metadata.summary: England's Charlotte Heath secured her maiden Ladies European Tour title in dramatic fashion, holding off a host of challengers to claim victory at the La Sella Open in Denia, Alicante.
metadata.content: La Sella Open 2026: Charlotte Heath bounces back after blowing four-shot lead to claim first LET title | Golf News | Sky Sports Skip to main content La Sella Open 2026: Charlotte Heath bounces back after blowing four-shot lead to claim first LET title Charlotte Heath clinched her debut Ladies European Tour title at the La Sella Open, bouncing back after letting a four-shot lead disappear to finish two shots clear of the field; watch LET golf live on Sky Sports Golf Sunday 20 September 2026 19:37, UK Image: England's Charlotte Heath claimed her debut Ladies European Tour victory at the La Sella Open England's Charlotte Heath secured her maiden Ladies European Tour title in dramatic fashion, holding off a host of challengers to claim victory at the La Sella Open in Denia, Alicante. The 24-year-old rookie started the final round with a four-shot advantage and, despite seeing her lead disappear during a tense Sunday afternoon, she held her composure to card a final-round 73 and finish at 10 under par, two shots clear of the field. After three weather-affected days, gusting winds continued to add an extra layer of difficulty, and set the stage for a thrilling finale at one of the LET's premier events. messages.text: DP World Tour plans to keep Play-Offs in UAE despite player safety concerns

metadata.summary: DP World Tour chief executive Guy Kinnings has confirmed that the plan is to keep the season-ending Play-Offs in the Middle East, despite ongoing conflict in the region.
metadata.content: DP World Tour chief executive Guy Kinnings confirms plan to stage Play-Offs in Middle East, despite player safety concerns | Golf News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Exclusive DP World Tour chief executive Guy Kinnings confirms plan to stage Play-Offs in Middle East, despite player safety concerns In an exclusive interview with Sky Sports, DP World Tour chief executive Guy Kinnings discussed the plans for the season-ending Play-Offs, the Strategic Alliance with the PGA Tour and the bright future the tour has within the global game By Ali Stafford at Wentworth Sunday 20 September 2026 15:01, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Matt Fitzpatrick voices his concerns over the DP World Tour Play-Offs in the Middle East DP World Tour chief executive Guy Kinnings has confirmed that the plan is to keep the season-ending Play-Offs in the Middle East, despite ongoing conflict in the region. The Abu Dhabi Championship is scheduled to be held at Yas Links on November 5-8, before the Race to Dubai season reaches its climax at the DP World Tour Championship the following week. There has been speculation throughout the season over whether both events would move to a different country, with Formula 1 cancelling two events earlier in the year in the region and discussions ongoing over whether races in Qatar and Abu Dhabi will go ahead.
